findings.text: the parity case's two sides both resolve through lane_document.read_lane_counts -- the left by a direct call, the right through the payload whose carry calls the same function on the same document -- so a regression inside read_lane_counts or its _GENERATING_KEYS list moves both sides together and leaves this assertion green; it does redden at base (AttributeError, my own base arm) and against a dispatch-side second reader growing back, but not against the module-side regression its docstring names, and the alias case at :230 is the assertion that actually carries that guard.

the lead sentence "the dispatch holds none of the document's names", and the figure caption at :71 reading "one module owns every key", are contradicted by the same fragment's section 2 table at :111-114 and by reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2661, :2692, :2693 and :2696 at the head, where the carry still reads four document keys itself; the claim holds for the generating and waiting counts and the rate block and not for the document as a whole, so a reader who takes the lead alone is told the opposite of the table three paragraphs below.
